correctness.rationale: Classical uniqueness plus permutation symmetry forces exactly a two-eigenvalue centered ellipsoid. Each of the d+2 halfspace constraints is evaluated by its exact support function; optimizing beta and center leaves the rigorously unimodal scalar objective R(1-2R)^((d-1)/2). This gives the unique formulas and contact threshold. Pairing inverse powers proves strict monotonicity of the full volume fraction for every a and d; finite standard-library tests reproduce supports, determinants, scalar optimum and sharp limit.

value.rationale: The affine-invariant maximal ellipsoid volume fraction and its contact-facet phase are natural quantitative descriptors of a simplex under a single-vertex truncation. The theorem completely determines both in all dimensions, including a sharp threshold and a strict global ordering, and exposes how a classical simplex extremizer persists and then changes as a genuinely new facet becomes binding. This is more than a substitution in an existing general contact condition or a numerical single-case table.
